name: The Hell Tithe

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
The Hell Tithe

At its heart, the Hell Tithe is a protection racket. As
detailed in Terrible Beauty, the Tithe is the faeries’
end of the bargain, under the threat of resuming the
ancient wars over mortal souls. Every seventh year
most communities of faeries deliver an agreed-upon
number of mortals to their infernal cousins’ wicked
claws, never to be seen again.
For all the faeries’ magic, wonderment, and
trickery, stealing away mortals is risky. Iron is ever
more plentiful in the mortal world, and every year
mortal magic and technological sophistication
grows yet more potent. Many faeries dream of a
brazen Wild Hunt to snatch their quota, but most
seek safer methods.
Mortal communities, especially in the
borderlands, are all too aware of their status
as prey for the fair folk even if they have no
understanding of why the faeries hunt them.
Thus, in the frontier are iron horseshoes hung at
doors, shrines to the Old Gods and Martyr alike
erected at crossroads, and discovered changelings
met with horror and fire.
The faeries risk their immortal lives to steal
mortals; mortals lose friends and loved ones to Hell;
the devils laugh all the while.

name: Stealing Lives

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Stealing Lives

Devils demand as many mortals as they think they
can convince, bribe, threaten, or blackmail their
faerie cousins into providing. These negotiations
are nasty, ugly things, as even the most amoral
faerie dislikes being strong-armed by their dark kin.
For their part, the devils push to oblige the faeries
as much as possible: if they come to ruin because
the quota is too severe, or because some disaster
displaces their mortal quarry, so much the better.
Devils demand different things. Some demand raw
numbers, expecting dozens or hundreds of mortals
in their tithe. Others are more exacting, expecting
only select mortals of some vanishingly rare quality,
deep Corruption, or satisfying some fleeting whim.
No matter the particulars, the result is always
calculated to be burdensome to the faerie and
horrific to the mortal alike.

name: Example Tithe-Takings

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Example Tithe-Takings

In addition to the above tables, you can roll or choose
results from the following table. Some combine
with the previous tables, while others will not. This
is intentional: the faeries are disunified at the best
of times, and you should take these examples as
inspiration for how to twist any results from the
previous tables as they please. Faeries go rogue and
splinter into factions with great frequency.
Many of these are inspired by real-world
mythologies, as there is no shortage of myths and
legends about people-stealers. If you’re looking
for additional inspiration, consider Japanese
yokai, Pacific Northwest skoocum, American UFO
abduction stories, and other boogeyman tales from
around the world.

Example

1

--- PDF p. 4 ---
d20

Example

17

A pixie (see Terrible Beauty) accompanies a small
puppy through town at dusk, watching for any
who would abuse the small animal, a barghest in
disguise. At night, they hunt together.

18

When a group of harvesters moved into this
community, they quickly ran afoul of the faeries
claiming it as their own and have been press
ganged to service of the elf lords.

19

The many changelings hidden in the community
serve the faeries a few nights a year, enchanted
to aid abductions. The enchantment is unravelling,
however, leaving a few changelings free-willed.

20

A local cliff, forest, or other popular place for
suicides is haunted by an opportunistic faerie,
offering despairing mortals all manner of bargains
and boons in exchange for a new purpose.
These mortals are empowered to drag their foes,
tormentors, or others off to the faeries or straight
to Hell itself.

name: Running the Tithe

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Running the Tithe
Most Hell Tithe scenarios where the characters are
cast as mortals feature the faeries in an antagonistic
role. Hell counts few allies in the realm of mortals, and
opposing the hunting and harvesting can unite even the
most disparate factions. Many of the faeries that carry
out the Tithe-Taking are just as monstrous as their devil
kin, after all. There are plenty of mortal foes in such a
story, too, as clandestine faerie pacts can empower those
willing to forsake their fellow mortals to the fires of Hell.

name: Listening to your Table

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Listening to your Table
Be mindful of your players’ comfort levels. The
thought of being abducted or having your child
stolen away with malicious intent is one of the
greatest horrors imaginable, and sadly all too
common in the real world. The Hell Tithe, for all
its supernatural elements, boils down to slavery
and human trafficking, and participating in that
simply isn’t many people’s idea of fun escapism.
Find other wrinkles if you wish to have your
games feature or focus on the Hell Tithe, such as
focusing on the wicked souls to be sent to Hell,
stopping the tithe-takers, or seeking revenge on
the faerie or devil alike.

Even those faeries who come to find a twisted joy
in the hunting of mortals or the cleverest of traps can
never forget that they are doing so to benefit Hell, not
themselves. Sneering devils make for good antagonists
in such a campaign, and every faerie dreams of finding
power or leverage enough to declare independence
from the Hell Tithe. Every faerie character in such a
story is likely to be looking for ways to subvert the Hell
Tithe, to give the devils as little as possible, or avoid
staining themselves with Corruption.
